todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Finish task 004 by recording removed-group cutoffs without manufacturing shared-conversation follows and by making follow causality group-aware so stale work from the removed group is rejected while same-generation work authorized through a surviving group remains valid.
scope: Revise the current task-004 candidate in place. Preserve its public Membership-to-Messaging cleanup boundary, Club-owned membership generation, Messaging-owned member eligibility cutoff, cleanup checkpoint barrier, success-only sender-follow policy, cleanup-id idempotency, and custom-group add/remove completion contract.

Fix the unfollowed shared-conversation branch. Cleanup must append one durable, idempotent removed-group cutoff even when another active group preserves access, but `ConversationUnfollowed.follow_retained` and the conversation-follow projection may retain only an aggregate follow that actually exists. An unfollowed member must remain unfollowed and notification-ineligible after cleanup.

Make each new conversation cleanup cutoff attributable to the removed group, and retain replay-compatible handling for historic cleanup facts without group/source fields. Ordinary user unfollow must continue to remove the follow without erasing durable cleanup cutoffs or completed cleanup IDs.

Carry durable authorizing/source-group information into follow-producing work. Manual current-member follow must retain the active conversation group or groups that authorized it; root sender follow uses its audience group; reply sender follow preserves the group-aware authorization context through the command/event and sender-follow policy instead of collapsing it to a club-wide generation.

Evaluate follow causality against removed-group cutoffs in `Memba.Messaging.ConversationFollowers`: work sourced only from removed group A at or before A's cutoff remains rejected, while work authorized through surviving group B is allowed at the same club generation. Apply the same rule to explicit manual follows and root/reply auto-follow paths, including aggregate replay of durable message/follow facts.

Add aggregate and integration coverage for a shared A+B conversation that was not followed at removal: record A's cutoff exactly once, keep aggregate and projected follow state false, and prove the member is not selected as a reply notification recipient.

Extend the shared-access race coverage with `remove A -> ordinary unfollow -> manual follow through B`, root sender follow through B, and reply-author follow through B, all without re-adding A or advancing the club generation. In the same causal model, prove delayed manual/root/reply work sourced only from A cannot restore the follow.

Keep and rerun existing proof for an already-followed shared conversation, unrelated conversations, manual/root/reply sources, genuinely newer post-re-add follows, cleanup-before-later-stream creation, projection lag and the interleaved stale-root checkpoint, replay/idempotency, caller-selected return modes, and Everyone/Admin no-ops.
scope_exclusions: Do not replace task 004 with a new task or reset its revision identity. All four prior candidate origins remain cumulative and unresolved until review accepts this obligation.

Do not weaken effective-access union semantics or require every conversation group to remain active. Surviving group B must continue to grant conversation access and may independently authorize a follow.

Do not solve the same-generation gap by globally allowing equality. Work sourced only from removed group A at its cutoff must remain rejected; the distinction must be represented by durable group/source-aware causality.

Do not make a projected row the authority for whether a follow exists, mutate projection tables directly, or coordinate ordering through transient process memory. Commands and backward-compatible facts remain authoritative.

Do not change task 001's accepted removal authorization, actor/target validation, self/last-member behavior, club role/membership preservation, system-group rejection, or `GroupMemberRemoved`-only transition semantics except for backward-compatible task-004 causal data.

Do not regress or redesign the packet-004 checkpoint barrier: enumeration must still wait through a durable Messaging checkpoint at or after `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded`, including an event-free exact retry.
Do not implement broader group/conversation query or action authorization, queued-delivery/provider-handoff reauthorization, or open-LiveView refresh assigned to tasks 009-011.
Do not add Leave/Remove UI, confirmations, shared member-row changes, post-removal screens, or empty-group UI behavior assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit iteration-064 feature files or implement the browser/domain acceptance layer assigned to tasks 015-016.
Do not redesign unrelated delivery, multi-group conversation editing, projection infrastructure, or club role lifecycle.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2 and the acceptance/open-technical-decision text require public Messaging APIs, idempotent facts, all follow sources, stale remove/re-add safety, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behavior.
Iteration 062 established the replay-safe Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration and requires departure/rejoin ordering; task 004 extends that boundary to explicit custom-group removal.
Membership owns group membership and Messaging owns follow state. Coordination uses public context APIs rather than another context's aggregates or projection storage.
The Club stream is authoritative for membership lifecycle and preserves historic facts; system-group membership remains a downstream policy consequence.

`clear_removed_group_member_follow/7` currently derives `retain_follow` from surviving access without checking current follow state. Manual and sender follow paths carry one club-wide generation; `establish_message_sender_follow/1` checks group-aware member eligibility but drops those group IDs before dispatching `FollowConversation`.

`ConversationFollowers` currently stores one cleanup generation per member. A cleanup command with surviving access emits `follow_retained=true` even for a non-follower, and every follow at or below that conversation-wide generation is rejected regardless of its authorizing group.
`FollowConversation` currently has no source-group field, so valid surviving-group work and stale removed-group work become indistinguishable at the aggregate boundary.
`UnfollowConversation` carries a cleanup ID, club-wide generation, and retention flag but not the removed group whose cutoff is being recorded.
The projector writes `ConversationUnfollowed.follow_retained` directly as projected `following`; a retained cleanup for a non-follower therefore inserts a phantom following row.

Member-level eligibility already records cutoffs by `{club_id, group_id}` and permits a follow through any surviving group. Conversation-level state must preserve equivalent source causality rather than overriding it with one member-wide cutoff.
The strong sender-follow policy runs after accepted root/reply facts. Preserve the authorizing group context through this durable path for both stale removed-group and valid surviving-group work.

The origin-replaying policy already supplies the removed group, Membership event identity, generation, and checkpoint to the public Messaging API. Preserve custom-group-only handling and direct Everyone/Admin no-ops.

Existing tests cover retained shared follows, older delayed work, newer post-re-add work, and the Messaging checkpoint interleaving. Extend them with an initially unfollowed shared conversation and same-generation manual/root/reply work through surviving group B versus stale work through removed group A.

Existing aggregate tests prove retained equal-generation cleanup and ordinary-unfollow cutoff preservation, but currently encode a conversation-wide cutoff. Add group/source-aware cutoff and historic absent-field replay cases.
Use projection coverage to prove a cleanup cutoff cannot create a following row for a member who was not following.
Commands/events remain the write authority; read projections must not decide or manufacture domain follow state.
Causal ordering and replay behavior must be represented by durable, backward-compatible facts rather than ephemeral workflow memory or projection-only state.
Use deterministic synchronization such as supervised processes, handler suspension, monitors, `Task.yield/2`, and state/barrier checks rather than sleeps.

constraints: Keep task identity 004 and revise the existing candidate; do not invent another task for the same rejected obligation.

Use Club-owned membership history as the causal source and Messaging-owned event-sourced state as the follow authority. Do not query another context's aggregate internals or directly write projection tables.
Represent new per-conversation cleanup and follow causality with removed/authorizing group identity or an equivalent durable source set; one club-wide generation alone is insufficient.

A cleanup may retain only an existing aggregate follow. It must still durably record the removed-group cutoff when no follow exists, while aggregate state, projection state, and reply notification eligibility remain false.

A follow is allowed at generation G when at least one captured authorizing group remains uncut at G; work sourced only from a group cut off at G is rejected. Do not require a club-generation advance to follow through an unchanged surviving group.

Capture root/reply/manual source context at the authoritative action boundary and carry it through durable commands/events as needed; do not infer causal authorization later from a potentially changed projection.
Ordinary user unfollow remains distinct from membership cleanup and must not erase group-specific or historic cleanup generations or completed cleanup IDs.

Preserve safe handling of historic `GroupMemberAdded`, `GroupMemberRemoved`, `MessageSent`, `ConversationFollowed`, `ConversationUnfollowed`, and cleanup shapes with absent generation/group/source/retention fields.
Preserve `ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` origin replay while ensuring ordinary projector reset/replay does not dispatch cross-context side effects.

Preserve successful public add/remove return semantics and cleanup completion for default, `:strong`, `:eventual`, explicit handler lists, event-free exact retry, and supported caller-selected Commanded return options.
Keep the deterministic interleaved-root checkpoint regression and avoid timing sleeps in new race tests.
Limit edits to durable group/source-aware follow cleanup semantics and focused tests. Leave tasks 009-017 untouched.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and describe the durable removed-group cutoff and authorizing/source-group data carried by cleanup, manual follow, root sender follow, and reply-author follow commands/events, including historic absent-field replay behavior.

Identify aggregate and projection tests proving cleanup records one idempotent cutoff for an initially unfollowed shared conversation without creating aggregate/projected follow state or reply-notification eligibility.

Identify tests proving `remove A -> ordinary unfollow -> manual follow through B`, root sender follow through B, and reply-author follow through B all succeed at the unchanged club generation, without re-adding A.

Identify paired tests proving delayed manual/root/reply work sourced only from removed group A at or before its cutoff cannot restore the follow, while genuinely newer post-re-add work remains allowed.

Show an already-followed shared conversation remains followed through surviving access, an unrelated-only conversation receives no cleanup fact, ordinary unfollow preserves cutoff history, and cleanup retry remains idempotent.

Show the existing deterministic test still proves a stale root committed between the Membership removal and `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded` is discovered only after projectors cross the Messaging checkpoint and ends without an effective follow.
Report exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands on the exact handoff state, plus `git diff --check`.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: explicit removal emits only the reusable Membership removal fact for a transition, exact retry emits no new Membership fact, and club membership/roles plus system-group guards are preserved.

latest_worker_result.summary: The candidate added retained shared-conversation cutoff facts and synchronized enumeration through the durable Messaging cleanup checkpoint, with reported 39- and 80-test focused suites passing; review found the remaining phantom-follow and source-insensitive same-generation cutoff gaps.
